paragraphs: AgentConductor studies how teams of language-model agents should communicate when solving competition-level coding problems. Fixed communication structures can create redundant exchanges, especially when they do not account for task difficulty or change in response to execution feedback. The paper makes the communication structure itself something the system can adapt.

An orchestrator trained with reinforcement learning infers useful agent roles and the difficulty of each query. It then constructs a layered directed acyclic graph describing agent interactions. A topology-density measure quantifies communication, while difficulty intervals help determine appropriate density upper bounds without excessively pruning the graph. Together, these mechanisms give the orchestrator finer control over how much collaboration a task receives.

Across five code datasets, the authors report improvements of up to 14.6% in pass@1 over the strongest baseline, alongside 13% lower topology density and 68% lower token cost. These results support adapting agent interactions through feedback as a way to improve coding performance while reducing communication and token use.
icml-2026-agentconductor-topology-evolut.tldr: AgentConductor adapts multi-agent communication to coding-task difficulty and execution feedback, improving reported performance while reducing token cost.

paragraphs: Generating an image once leaves little room to correct mistakes in complex prompts. This paper formalizes a repeated Reason–Reflect–Rectify process: reason about the task, assess the generated result, and produce instructions for correction. It introduces R³-Bench, containing more than 600 expert-annotated instances, to evaluate the reasoning and correction abilities needed for this process.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a specific gap: the evaluated leading models can recognize generation errors but struggle to turn that recognition into actionable editing instructions. R³-Refiner addresses this gap through two stages of training that use Group Relative Policy Optimization and a hierarchical reward mechanism. The aim is to connect reflective judgments more closely to useful corrective actions.

The authors report improvements of 12.0% in Reflective Verdict Score and 9.0% in Rectification Score on R³-Bench. They also report improved image-generation quality on GenEval++ and T2I-CompBench when integrating the refiner with different multimodal and image-generation models. The findings emphasize that identifying an error and explaining how to fix it are distinct capabilities.
icml-2026-benchmarking-and-evolving-reas.tldr: R³-Bench evaluates iterative visual correction, and R³-Refiner trains models to turn detected image errors into more useful correction instructions.

paragraphs: CLARITree targets regression trees that make linear predictions within different regions of the input space. These models combine readable decision rules with more expressive local predictions. Building them efficiently is difficult: greedy construction is common, but more thorough optimization can produce substantially better trees at a computational cost that becomes prohibitive.

The proposed algorithm combines a search strategy that looks ahead at future choices with efficient updates to the linear-algebra calculations used during fitting. Specifically, it uses rank-one Cholesky updates of the Gram matrix. These updates let the procedure revise relevant computations as the search progresses, helping make a more deliberate search practical for sparse, piecewise linear regression trees.

The paper provides theoretical and empirical evidence for a favorable balance among runtime, predictive accuracy, and sparsity, and reports substantially better scaling than the current state of the art. Its contribution is a near-optimal construction method: the claim concerns approaching strong solutions efficiently, rather than guaranteeing the exact best tree in every case.
icml-2026-claritree-cholesky-and-lookahe.tldr: CLARITree combines lookahead search with efficient matrix updates to build sparse, near-optimal piecewise linear regression trees.

paragraphs: Evolution strategies improve a search distribution by evaluating candidate solutions and favoring better performers. When evaluations are noisy, candidate rankings can be wrong. Under a fixed budget, spending more evaluations to clarify each ranking leaves fewer opportunities to update the search distribution. This paper investigates that trade-off between ranking reliability and optimization depth.

Probabilistic elite membership replaces weights based on a single noisy ranking with expected rank weights that account for ranking uncertainty. The authors show that this preserves the conditional mean of the update while reducing its conditional dispersion, a statistical averaging operation known as Rao–Blackwellization. Their practical version, RB-PEM, uses residual bootstrapping with capped overhead and adds an adaptive probe-and-switch mechanism for low-noise settings.

Experiments cover the COCO bbob-noisy suite, reinforcement-learning policy search, and hyperparameter optimization. RB-PEM shows consistent gains where misranking is substantial and evaluation budgets are constrained. The finding supports handling uncertainty within the update rule so that more of the available budget can support successive optimization steps.
icml-2026-depth-over-fidelity-in-fixed-b.tldr: RB-PEM accounts for uncertain candidate rankings to improve noisy evolution strategies when evaluation budgets are tight and misranking is substantial.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks commonly exchange information along the connections already present in a graph. Those connections may omit meaningful relationships between nodes. DCD-GNN addresses this problem by learning through two parallel channels: one preserves the supplied graph structure, and the other learns an adaptive adjacency structure that can represent additional semantic relationships.

The dynamic channel uses self-attention to learn adjacency and combines two complementary views. Low-pass filtering captures shared structural information, while high-pass filtering preserves more individualized details. The static channel maintains structural stability alongside this adaptation. Both channels fuse representations across multiple scales, and their outputs are combined into a single node representation intended to distinguish nodes effectively.

The authors report superior discriminative graph-representation learning across several benchmark datasets. The approach matters because structural preservation and relationship discovery have separate roles within the same model. Its reported findings support combining the original graph with learned connections and complementary filtering views, rather than relying entirely on a fixed adjacency structure.
icml-2026-dual-channel-dynamic-graph-neu.tldr: DCD-GNN combines a structure-preserving graph channel with learned connections and complementary filters to improve node representations.

paragraphs: Black-box optimization methods need benchmarks that meaningfully test their search behavior. Human-designed benchmarks can reflect expert preferences and offer limited diversity. Evolution of Benchmark, or EoB, automates benchmark construction by using a language model to evolve programs that define optimization problems. The benchmark itself becomes the object of an optimization process.

EoB pursues two objectives together: resemblance to the landscapes of target tasks and the ability to distinguish among a portfolio of optimization algorithms. It repeatedly prompts a language model to modify a population of benchmark programs. A reflection-based process co-evolves the program and its resulting landscape, connecting changes in implementation to the properties of the problem being generated.

Experiments present EoB as a competitive option for comparing black-box optimizers, training and evaluating learning-assisted optimizers, and extending proxies for expensive real-world problems. The contribution is a way to generate benchmarks with explicit design goals, making both target relevance and solver differentiation part of the construction process.
icml-2026-evolution-of-benchmark-black-b.tldr: EoB uses language-model program evolution to create optimization benchmarks that resemble target tasks and distinguish among solvers.

paragraphs: Sharpness-Aware Minimization trains a model by considering the worst loss near its current parameters. The usual method defines that neighborhood with a fixed radius in parameter space. This paper points out a mismatch: SAM commonly relies on a first-order approximation, while the flatness it seeks is fundamentally about second-order curvature.

Loss-Equated SAM changes what stays fixed during the perturbation step. Instead of imposing a constant distance in parameter space, it uses a fixed budget in loss space. According to the authors, this removes learning signals dominated by gradient magnitude and shifts optimization toward curvature-dominated terms. That change directly targets the mismatch between the approximation used to construct perturbations and the geometry motivating the method.

Across diverse benchmarks and tasks, the authors report that LE-SAM consistently generalizes better than SAM and its variants, reaching state-of-the-art performance in their experiments. The stated results support loss-based perturbation control as an effective route to sharper attention to curvature during training.
icml-2026-fix-the-loss-not-the-radius-re.tldr: LE-SAM replaces a fixed parameter-space perturbation radius with a fixed loss budget to emphasize curvature and improve reported generalization.

paragraphs: Medical dialogue presents a difficult reinforcement-learning problem because a good response depends on context and cannot easily be summarized by a simple reward. ORBIT addresses this with evaluation rubrics generated for individual cases. These rubrics provide adaptive guidance for incremental training, connecting feedback to the particular medical conversation being learned.

The framework combines dialogue construction with rubric-guided evaluation. It can use general-purpose instruction-following language models without specialized judge fine-tuning, external medical knowledge bases, or handcrafted rules. Its central design choice is to make the evaluation criteria responsive to the case, giving the training process more structured guidance for an open-ended task with ambiguous feedback.

Using 2,000 training samples, ORBIT raises Qwen3-4B-Instruct’s HealthBench-Hard score from 7.0 to 27.5. The authors report state-of-the-art performance among similarly sized open-source models and strong consultation quality as rubric coverage expands. These findings show substantial benchmark gains from case-conditioned feedback and incremental training in the evaluated medical-dialogue setting.
icml-2026-infimed-orbit-aligning-llms-on.tldr: ORBIT uses dynamically generated medical-case rubrics to guide incremental reinforcement learning, substantially improving a small model’s HealthBench-Hard score.

paragraphs: Machine learning interatomic potentials support accurate molecular-dynamics simulations, but scaling their training presents a distinctive systems problem. Conservative models compute gradients within their forward pass, creating a double-backward execution pattern. Distributed training systems designed around more conventional execution do not naturally accommodate this pattern, particularly when model stages are spread across a pipeline.

JanusPipe is a three-dimensional parallel training system tailored to these conservative models. Its SymFold component enables memory-efficient pipeline parallelism. Its WaveK component balances computation across four phases to reduce pipeline bubbles, the periods when parts of the pipeline are idle. These components address both the memory demands and scheduling imbalance created by the unusual execution pattern.

In experiments using 32 GPUs, JanusPipe delivers average throughput improvements of 1.51 times over 1F1B and 1.45 times over Hanayo. The contribution is a training-system design that matches the computation of conservative interatomic potentials, making the reported scaling benefits a consequence of specialized execution and scheduling.
icml-2026-januspipe-efficient-pipeline-p.tldr: JanusPipe adapts distributed training to conservative interatomic potentials’ double-backward computation, improving throughput in 32-GPU experiments.

paragraphs: This paper examines why language models struggle in unfamiliar environments involving symbolic or spatial tasks. The authors identify expensive exploration as the primary bottleneck in their study: learning these environments requires extensive trial and error, which is costly for large models operating through a high-dimensional semantic space.

SCOUT separates collecting experience from using it. Small models, such as lightweight multilayer perceptrons, act as scouts that probe environmental dynamics quickly and at scale. Their collected trajectories then provide supervised fine-tuning data for the language model. Multi-turn reinforcement learning follows, with the aim of activating the language model’s latent world knowledge after it has received an initial foundation of experience.

The authors report that SCOUT enables Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct to achieve an average score of 0.86, compared with 0.60 for Gemini-2.5-Pro, while saving about 60% in GPU hours. The result supports allocating exploratory interaction to inexpensive models and transferring that experience into a language model as an effective strategy in the evaluated tasks.
icml-2026-language-based-trial-and-error.tldr: SCOUT uses lightweight models to gather exploratory experience, then trains a language model on it to improve unfamiliar-task performance at lower computational cost.

paragraphs: Generative image steganography hides secret images within images produced by a diffusion model. The paper identifies three problems with existing approaches: a fixed hiding space limits capacity, multiple secrets interfere when placed in the same space, and receivers lack a verification mechanism. Its framework addresses capacity allocation and receiver authentication together.

A dynamic cover-selection and optimization component assigns suitable hiding spaces to different secret images. It can distribute either separate images or fragments of one image across distinct spaces. This separation is designed to prevent interference between secrets while increasing total capacity. A signature controller then cryptographically signs the secret container after concealment and checks it before extraction, supporting receiver isolation and identification of the relevant container.

The experiments report strong large-capacity generative steganography and superior secure isolation among multiple receivers. The approach matters because accommodating more hidden content also requires managing how secrets share space and how receivers verify the containers from which they extract that content.
icml-2026-large-capacity-and-receiver-au.tldr: The framework combines adaptive hiding-space allocation with signed secret containers to support higher-capacity image steganography and receiver verification.

paragraphs: Generating realistic EEG signals could help address limited data and privacy constraints in neural modeling. This paper argues that discrete denoising objectives poorly reflect the continuous temporal dynamics and spectral structure of EEG. The resulting mismatch can make it difficult to preserve long-range relationships and reproduce the structure of real signals.

Just EEG Transformer, or JET, uses conditional flow matching on raw EEG sequences. It learns a smooth vector field that transforms noise toward the EEG data distribution along continuous trajectories. The framework also introduces constraints on spectral structure, temporal stationarity, and signal-level statistics. These constraints guide the learned dynamics toward relevant EEG properties without requiring domain-specific signal representations.

Across three large-scale benchmarks, JET achieves reported state-of-the-art performance and reduces TS-FID by more than 40% relative to strong baselines. Additional analyses find that it captures key structural properties of neural dynamics. Together, these findings support continuous generative modeling with explicit signal constraints for improving EEG synthesis.
icml-2026-let-eeg-models-learn-eeg-a730e.tldr: JET generates raw EEG through continuous flow matching with signal-preserving constraints, reducing TS-FID by over 40% in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Integrated-circuit footprint labeling describes the physical interface between a component and a printed circuit board. Extracting this geometry from mechanical drawings requires precise visual interpretation, but the drawings and their abstract annotations are often unstructured. The paper targets the geometric perception errors that limit general multimodal models on this task.

LMM4-IC4K treats the mechanical drawings as images and trains a large multimodal model to produce structured geometric interpretations. To support this work, the authors introduce ICGeo8K, a dataset of 8,608 labeled examples: 4,138 real-world footprint samples and 4,470 synthetic samples. A two-stage fine-tuning framework adapts the models specifically for footprint labeling.

Experiments show that the resulting model outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal models on the proposed benchmark. The work connects specialized visual training data with a concrete engineering interpretation task. Its stated contribution to PCB automation and standardization comes from translating footprint diagrams more accurately into structured geometric information that defines how components physically connect to boards.
icml-2026-lmm4-ic4k-a-large-multimodal-m.tldr: LMM4-IC4K combines a specialized dataset and two-stage fine-tuning to improve structured geometry extraction from integrated-circuit footprint drawings.

paragraphs: In a system of collaborating language-model agents, each agent typically receives a prompt describing its role. Improving those prompts independently can miss what makes the whole system succeed: an agent’s locally acceptable output may provide poor input for the agents that follow. MASPO tackles this mismatch by optimizing prompts jointly across the system.

Its evaluation mechanism judges prompts partly by whether they enable downstream agents to succeed, connecting local interactions to overall outcomes without requiring ground-truth labels. The framework repeatedly refines prompts and uses a data-driven evolutionary beam search to explore the many possible combinations. This makes prompt selection sensitive to the way agents depend on one another.

Across six diverse tasks, the authors report that MASPO consistently beats state-of-the-art prompt optimization methods, with an average accuracy improvement of 2.9. The result supports evaluating prompts as parts of an interacting workflow. The central contribution is making downstream usefulness an explicit criterion for automatic prompt improvement.
icml-2026-maspo-joint-prompt-optimizatio.tldr: MASPO jointly improves multi-agent prompts by evaluating how well each prompt supports downstream success.

paragraphs: Medical vision-language models can produce unsupported statements when interpreting images. Editing their internal activations offers a relatively inexpensive way to reduce these hallucinations, but generic editing methods can miss the imaging findings and diagnostic principles needed for medical interpretation. MEDA introduces medical guidance into this activation-editing approach.

The method combines two components. Query-decisive Manifestation Steering retrieves positive imaging manifestations relevant to the question and uses them as trusted guidance for steering activations. Principle-driven Diagnosis Induction constructs positive diagnostic prompts that incorporate medical principles to encourage expert-like reasoning. Together, they aim to elicit relevant model expertise through both image-related evidence and diagnostic guidance.

The authors evaluate MEDA across six benchmarks and six vision-language models. They report improved response factuality, including gains of up to 10.2% on IU-Xray, alongside strong generalization and robustness with few examples. These findings support tailoring activation editing to the evidence and reasoning demands of the medical domain in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-meda-medical-oriented-activati.tldr: MEDA uses question-relevant imaging findings and diagnostic principles to guide activation editing and improve medical vision-language response factuality.

paragraphs: Learning a shared feature extractor usually involves training on all related data sources while giving each source its own prediction head. This paper asks whether using every source is necessary even when the sources appear similarly relevant and similarly good. Its focus goes beyond the familiar problem of filtering out obviously poor data.

For tractability, the analysis considers a linear setting in which sources share a low-dimensional subspace. The authors show that, for a broad class of problem instances, a carefully selected subset of sources is sufficient for minimax-optimal subspace estimation. This means achieving the best worst-case statistical performance in the analyzed setting can remain possible even after discarding a substantial portion of the data.

The paper formalizes what makes a subpopulation informative and develops algorithms and practical heuristics for finding such subsets. Theory and experiments on synthetic and real-world data support their effectiveness. The finding makes source selection a substantive part of representation learning, including among collections already regarded as good.
icml-2026-on-the-power-of-source-screeni.tldr: For a broad class of linear shared-subspace problems, carefully selected source subsets suffice for statistically optimal estimation despite substantial data removal.

paragraphs: Offline policy evaluation estimates how a policy would perform using previously collected data. In a network, one person’s outcome can depend on neighbors’ treatments as well as their own, violating the usual no-interference assumption. This paper models that dependence through a unified exposure mapping, including an aggregation that gives more distant neighbors decaying influence.

A second problem arises when the target policy would produce situations insufficiently represented by the policy that collected the data. In these non-overlap regions, the policy value cannot be identified as a single number. The method instead seeks lower and upper bounds. Under a smoothness assumption, it expresses their estimation as a linear program that yields valid bounds on the offline policy value.

Experiments on semi-synthetic network data assess effectiveness and robustness when interference and limited overlap occur together. The contribution is an evaluation framework that accounts for both social spillovers and incomplete data coverage, expressing the resulting uncertainty through bounds rather than an unsupported point estimate.
icml-2026-partial-identification-of-poli.tldr: The method bounds offline policy values under network interference and limited overlap, using a smoothness assumption to formulate a linear program.

paragraphs: Mechanistic interpretability investigates how a trained network’s internal structure produces its behavior. Patterning reverses that direction of inquiry: given a desired kind of generalization, it asks which changes to training data would encourage it. The paper develops a mathematical connection between changing the data distribution and steering internal model structure.

Its central quantities are susceptibilities, which describe how posterior expectations of observable properties respond to infinitesimal changes in the data distribution. Inverting this linear response relationship yields a data intervention directed toward a target internal configuration. In a small language model, reweighting data along principal susceptibility directions can speed up or delay structural development, including formation of an induction circuit.

On a synthetic parentheses-balancing task, multiple algorithms reach perfect training accuracy. The authors show that targeting the local learning coefficient of each solution can influence which algorithm the model learns. These demonstrations establish a route from measuring internal structure to intentionally shaping it through training-data weights.
icml-2026-patterning-the-dual-of-interpr.tldr: Patterning inverts a mathematical response relationship to choose training-data changes that steer a model’s internal structures and learned algorithms.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning trains policies entirely from fixed datasets, making generalization under distribution shift a central concern. This paper examines the geometry of the training loss, particularly whether seeking flatter solutions can help. Applying Sharpness-Aware Minimization directly is difficult because value-learning targets are bootstrapped, making estimates of sharpness noisy and potentially destabilizing training.

Q-SAM adapts sharpness-aware optimization to this setting by weighting the objective at the sample level. It uses Q bounds to prioritize samples that are more suitable for sharpness-aware updates. This selective weighting aims to preserve the benefits of minimizing sharpness while accommodating the uncertainty associated with bootstrapped value estimation and maintaining training stability.

Experiments on standard offline reinforcement-learning benchmarks show consistent generalization improvements across varied datasets and algorithms. The findings support treating optimizer design as an additional route to stronger offline learning. In particular, they show reported benefits from adapting sharpness minimization to the structure of value estimation rather than transferring it unchanged from supervised learning.
icml-2026-q-sam-unlocking-sharpness-awar.tldr: Q-SAM weights sharpness-aware updates using Q bounds to improve offline reinforcement-learning generalization while preserving training stability.

paragraphs: Many networks contain several kinds of relationships, represented as separate layers. Treating each layer independently can miss dependencies between them, while combining them into one graph can also lose that structure. T-GINEE introduces a statistical regularization framework that explicitly represents cross-layer correlations alongside the loss for the task being solved.

The method uses CP tensor decomposition to express structural dependencies through shared latent factors. Generalized estimating equations incorporate inter-layer relationships through working covariance matrices, and a flexible link function accommodates properties such as sparsity. These components give the framework separate ways to capture shared structure, model statistical dependence, and adapt to characteristics of the observed network.

Under conditions described as mild, the theoretical analysis establishes consistency and asymptotic normality. Those are conditional large-sample guarantees about estimation behavior. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets also support the method’s effectiveness. Together, the results motivate explicitly modeling correlations between relationship layers when learning representations of multilayer networks.
icml-2026-t-ginee-a-tensor-based-multila.tldr: T-GINEE combines tensor decomposition and statistical estimating equations to learn multilayer graph representations with explicit cross-layer correlations.

paragraphs: Group Relative Policy Optimization has shown promise for training flow-matching image and video generators, but this paper finds that direct transfer to image-to-video generation does not consistently improve rewards. TAGRPO addresses that instability through a contrastive approach to post-training, using comparisons between better and worse generated video trajectories.

The method builds on the observation that videos generated from the same initial noise provide better optimization guidance. Its loss operates on intermediate latent representations, encouraging alignment with high-reward trajectories and separation from low-reward ones. This brings the training signal into the trajectory itself. A memory bank of rollout videos adds diversity while reducing the computational overhead of obtaining training examples.

The authors report significant improvements over DanceGRPO in image-to-video generation. The contribution is a simple way to adapt reward-guided optimization to this generation setting: compare trajectories from matched initial noise, steer intermediate representations according to their rewards, and reuse rollout videos to make the process more efficient.
icml-2026-tagrpo-boosting-grpo-on-image-.tldr: TAGRPO improves image-to-video post-training by aligning intermediate latents with high-reward trajectories and separating them from low-reward counterparts.

paragraphs: Multi-target domain adaptation learns from one labeled domain and several unlabeled target domains. U³CF argues that simply encouraging domain-invariant representations can bias adaptation across targets. It introduces a structural causal formulation that distinguishes invariant causal factors from domain-specific factors, with the latter producing spurious relationships with labels across target domains.

The framework aligns domains through semantic prototypes, updating them progressively using high-confidence target predictions. A contrastive objective brings target samples toward the appropriate prototypes while preserving class distinctions. It also separates representations into invariant causal components and domain-specific confounders. Conditional intervention blocks the confounding effects while retaining invariant semantics, and a criterion derived from mutual information guides feature separation.

Across four benchmarks, U³CF consistently outperforms leading methods in the reported experiments. Its contribution connects multi-domain alignment with an explicit account of which information should be preserved and which effects should be blocked. The causal formulation and prototype alignment work together to support predictions across multiple unlabeled targets.
icml-2026-u-3-cf-unbiased-unconfounding-.tldr: U³CF combines semantic-prototype alignment with causal feature separation and conditional intervention to improve adaptation across multiple target domains.

paragraphs: Language-model alignment often learns from comparisons expressing which response people prefer. Real preference datasets contain substantial noise, which can distort training through reward models or Direct Preference Optimization. This paper develops a theoretical framework for correcting that distortion within the training objective, allowing learning directly from noisy preferences.

The authors introduce two losses: Unbiased Reward Model loss for reward-model training and Unbiased Direct Preference Optimization loss for direct alignment. Both mathematically adjust for preference-noise distortion without requiring clean ground-truth supervision. Their analyses establish noise tolerance, parameter downward compatibility, and classification calibration. The correction is therefore presented with formal properties as well as a practical training objective.

Experiments across diverse datasets show the proposed approaches outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The work’s significance is that unreliable preference labels can be addressed through the loss used to learn from them. Its stated theoretical contribution provides a basis for unbiased alignment within the proposed framework, while the experiments demonstrate practical benefits in the evaluated datasets.
icml-2026-unbiased-alignment-for-large-l.tldr: URM and UDPO correct preference-noise distortion in alignment losses, enabling theoretically unbiased training without clean ground-truth supervision.

paragraphs: Removing visual tokens can accelerate vision-language models, but this paper finds that the safety effects depend strongly on the pruning strategy. Most evaluated strategies become less safe as pruning increases. Query-based compression shows the opposite pattern, with pruning as high as 99.8% unexpectedly improving safety in the reported evaluation.

The authors identify a mechanism in which removing background tokens concentrates attention on a few malicious foreground anchors during a jailbreak. This amplifies their harmful semantic influence. Safety-Aware Pruning addresses the mechanism at inference time by identifying those anchors, restoring benign tokens that were removed, and shifting excessive attention from the malicious anchors toward benign content.

Across three safety benchmarks and four utility benchmarks, the method reduces attack success rate by up to 62% without compromising efficiency or utility in the reported experiments. The findings show that pruning changes more than computational cost: which visual information remains can reshape how strongly harmful content influences the model’s response.
icml-2026-understanding-and-mitigating-t.tldr: Safety-Aware Pruning counteracts attention concentration on malicious visual tokens, reducing pruning-related attack success without reported efficiency or utility losses.

paragraphs: Prior-data Fitted Networks promise causal-effect estimates without tuning a model separately for each dataset. This paper investigates whether unified pretraining can support general interventions on subsets of variables in structural causal models. It identifies a theoretical coverage problem that challenges the effectiveness of current pretraining approaches in this setting.

The authors prove that one observational causal model induces an exponentially large space of interventional distributions. They call the resulting coverage failure prior uncoverage. This creates a mismatch between the learned meta-prior and the true grounding prior, producing unavoidable posterior inconsistency and estimation bias in their analysis. The issue concerns how well pretraining covers the intervention distribution needed for a particular causal estimate.

The paper argues that fine-tuning is fundamentally necessary to address this problem. Point-Wise Interventional Fine-tuning targets a particular intervention and enables local generalization. Meta-Sampling Fine-tuning extends the approach through budgeted active learning, with the stated result of uniform generalization across any interventional distribution in the analyzed framework.
icml-2026-unveiling-prior-data-fitted-ne.tldr: The paper identifies intervention-prior coverage limits in causal PFN pretraining and proposes targeted and meta-sampling fine-tuning to address them.
